about: Lesson F6, overfitting and the held-out set. Computed by tools/school/fill_heldout.mjs from system/school/heldout.mjs, backprop.mjs and the attention lab's model.json. Do not edit by hand.

poly.about: Least-squares polynomials of degree 0 to 15 fitted to 16 noisy samples of sin(pi x) on [-1, 1] (Gaussian noise, sigma 0.2; x uniform; seed 21), scored by root-mean-square error on those points, on 500 held-out samples from the same source (seed 22), and against the noise-free curve on 401 grid points. Degree 15 has 16 coefficients for 16 points, so it passes through every one. Solved by Householder QR on the design matrix (ridge: QR on the matrix stacked over sqrt(lambda) times the identity, constant term unpenalised). 'residual' is the relative residual of the normal equations; 'rDiagRatio' is max|R_jj| / min|R_jj|, a lower bound on the condition number.

curves.about: Fitted curves on 161 points over [-1, 1] for the film; the high degrees swing far outside the data, so a view should clip.

controls.about: The transposed control solves A^T c = y for the square degree-15 system and must fail the normal-equation residual check. The Cholesky rows form A^T A and solve it; both routes satisfy the normal equations to rounding, but forming A^T A squares the condition number and the fit to the 16 points shows it.

spread.about: 200 training draws (seeds 1000 to 1199), held-out set fixed: held-out RMSE at degree 3 and 15 (5th percentile, median, 95th), train RMSE at 15, and how often each degree is the best on held-out data.

spiral.about: The F4 spiral net (2, 8, 8, 2, tanh) trained with plain SGD (step 0.3, minibatch 32 drawn with replacement, batch seed 5, net seed 3) for 10000 updates on 40 points and, as the control, on 400. The 40 points are the first 40 of the 400 (seed 1). Held-out: 400 points from seed 2. Curves every 100 updates.

draws.about: Five different 40-point training draws (seeds 1, 11, 21, 31, 41), everything else fixed.

attention.about: The attention lab's model. 'curve' is model.json's own: 'train' is the mean loss of the training batches of the previous 25 updates, each measured before its update; 'heldOut' is the loss on the 256 held-out rows after the update. The trainer draws a fresh batch from the generator every update; the generator's small grammar repeats some rows by chance ('repeats' counts them), so rows are rarely, not never, seen twice. Much of the gap is that the train number averages a model that was still improving. 'rescored' takes the final weights and scores them, the same way, on rows they were trained on (the batches of updates 1 to 16, and of the last 16 updates), on the next 16 batches of the same stream (never trained on), on the lab's 256 held-out rows, and on five fresh 256-row draws with other seeds, which give the spread of an unseen score.
